reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting guaranteed extraction from Windsurf or Trae: the README says their undocumented SQLite formats are parsed with a heuristic that can return zero conversations after a schema change.

reviews.name: RuVector
reviews.verdict: RuVector is worth testing for an embedded agent-memory system when you can start with `VectorDB` or the hooks CLI and ignore most of the monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting one stable facade over every memory type: the README says the unified manager lacks native save and load, and cross-type consolidation is incomplete.

reviews.name: crw
reviews.verdict: fastCRW is a credible choice when one compact service must feed web data to applications and MCP agents, particularly for teams testing a move from Firecrawl.
reviews.skip_if: Teams scraping heavily protected sites as a hard requirement: open issue #189 documents CARFAX content being blocked by client-side bot detection even with Chromium.

reviews.name: prettymaps
reviews.verdict: Prettymaps remains a delightful shortcut from a place name to distinctive map art, and its returned data and Matplotlib objects keep it from being a toy.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that need deterministic offline rendering: initial map queries depend on OpenStreetMap services, and issue #150 reports an Overpass connection failure with no response yet.

reviews.name: qlib
reviews.verdict: Our Qlib run installed 214 packages and built successfully; 10 tests failed and 9 more ended in collection or setup errors, so it suits quant research teams that can validate the stack themselves.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a dependable market dataset in the download: the README says the official dataset is temporarily disabled, points to a community archive, and warns that its Yahoo-derived data may be imperfect.

reviews.name: ai-data-extraction
reviews.verdict: Use this toolkit as a transparent starting point for a personal, offline recovery job, not as proof that you now have a complete training corpus.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a verified lossless backup: the README concedes that deleted, corrupted, response-less, or otherwise partial conversations may be missing, and the repository has no test suite.

reviews.name: chinese-poetry-api
reviews.verdict: Chinese Poetry API is an appealing ready-made backend for a Chinese poetry product, especially when full-text search and traditional-character output matter.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require English documentation: the README, API explanations, and load-testing guide are written primarily in Chinese.

reviews.name: czsc
reviews.verdict: CZSC is a serious and unusually deep implementation for researchers who specifically want Chan theory, not a general recommendation for anyone doing technical analysis.
reviews.skip_if: English-only developers who need first-party tutorials and reference material: the README, public API guide, changelog, examples, issue discussion, and linked community resources are primarily Chinese.

reviews.name: flights
reviews.verdict: fast-flights is a clever, convenient starting point for personal tools and prototypes, especially when a few typed lines of Python are more valuable than contractual reliability.
reviews.skip_if: Booking, expense, or customer-facing systems that require complete and dependable itineraries: issue #97 documents missing self-transfer results and price differences, while issue #101 reports expected results not being parsed.

reviews.name: MediaCrawler
reviews.verdict: MediaCrawler is useful source material and a workable research collector for the Chinese platforms it knows, provided you accept interactive login and breakage when sites change.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial data operations: the custom license permits non-commercial learning and research, and forbids commercial use without written consent.

reviews.name: pgrust
reviews.verdict: Do not put production data in pgrust, but do take the project seriously.
reviews.skip_if: Any production workload or valuable data: the README explicitly says pgrust is not production-ready and still has many bugs.

reviews.name: v
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run commit 4ddbd6c because V is outside the lab's supported ecosystems, so this review cannot confirm the README's quick source-build story.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require a frozen language and standard-library API: the README says breaking language changes and minor core API changes may happen before 1.0.

reviews.name: autoprompt-skill
reviews.verdict: Our AutoPrompt test command finished with 78 of 80 tests passing and still exited 1, so version 1.0.4 is not a clean lab pass.
reviews.skip_if: Small edits where several agents cost more time than the change deserves: the README estimates about 3 times the time and 2 times the tokens, without retained logs for those estimates.

reviews.name: gitbutler
reviews.verdict: GitButler is worth trying if stacked branches and constant commit surgery consume a meaningful part of your week.
reviews.skip_if: Companies building a competing Git client or service: the Functional Source License forbids competing use for two years after each version is published.

reviews.name: no-mistakes
reviews.verdict: No Mistakes has a sharp idea and a polished workflow, especially for solo developers who already rely on coding agents.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a proven enforcement boundary before code reaches GitHub: an open report says a test analyzer that never ran could be recorded as passed, allowing a failing new test through green checks.

reviews.name: pdfcn
reviews.verdict: pdfcn is an appealing shortcut for React teams that need polished invoices and reports and are comfortable owning copied component code.
reviews.skip_if: Non-React projects or teams committed to HTML-to-PDF: the installation guide requires a React project that can run Takumi or Forme.

reviews.name: dsh-web-ui
reviews.verdict: dsh-web-ui is the most compelling add-on bundle for an enthusiastic DSH user who wants the web interface to become a full workbench.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not already run DeepSeek Harness: every feature mounts into the `dsh web` profile, so this is not a standalone coding agent.

reviews.name: union
reviews.verdict: Union is serious protocol infrastructure for teams that specifically want light-client-based interoperability and can evaluate its chain-specific code.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers seeking one small bridge library: this repository includes the chain, prover, relayer, contracts, sites, and several SDK workspaces.

reviews.name: atlas
reviews.verdict: Atlas is one of the more coherent attempts to make multiple coding agents feel like participants in the same project instead of isolated chat windows.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users seeking a supported desktop build: the README supports macOS downloads and calls builds for the other two platforms untested.

reviews.name: hop
reviews.verdict: HOP is already useful as a free cross-platform HWP viewer and cautious light editor, especially on macOS and Linux where first-party choices are limited.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who must edit and save HWPX files: the development guide says HWPX opens, but saving is blocked until a safe serializer is ready.

reviews.name: RustPython
reviews.verdict: RustPython is a compelling component when Rust embedding or WebAssembly is the actual requirement, not merely a preference.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting drop-in CPython compatibility, because current issues document mismatches in builtins, inspection, CSV, annotations, and diagnostics Scientific Python users relying on CPython native extensions and its full binary ecosystem Teams wanting a polished installer, because the README says installation…

reviews.name: microsandbox
reviews.verdict: Our microsandbox build ran for 347 seconds before `-lcap-ng` stopped the linker, and the test build hit the same native-library requirement, so contributor setup is heavier than the one-command user demo.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts without supported virtualization: Linux requires KVM, Windows requires Windows Hypervisor Platform, and macOS support is limited to Apple silicon.

reviews.name: writer-computer
reviews.verdict: Writer is easy to recommend to an Apple Silicon Mac owner who wants Markdown to feel like a writing app without surrendering plain files.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, Intel Mac, or older x86_64 Mac users seeking an official binary: every current release asset is for Apple Silicon macOS, and the release guide explicitly excludes other targets.

reviews.name: OpenCADStudio
reviews.verdict: Our Open CAD Studio release build completed in 459 seconds, but its test build stopped on a missing `mesh_from_solid` function, so version 0.9.7 is better suited to evaluated copies than sole-source production drawings.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot risk drawing corruption or incomplete behavior: the README explicitly says the project is under active development and tells users to back up important production files.

reviews.name: DevOps-Interview-Guide
reviews.verdict: Use DevOps Interview Guide as a stack of flash cards, especially when your target company appears in the folders.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for explanations or model answers: the files are question lists, and the README does not claim to teach the underlying topics.

reviews.name: DesktopCommanderMCP
reviews.verdict: Our Desktop Commander install ran for 900 seconds without completing, so we could not build or test the 301-file checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating `allowedDirectories` or the command blocklist as a security boundary: the project says terminal commands can bypass both.

reviews.name: claude-ads
reviews.verdict: Claude Ads is unusually disciplined for an agent skill: its evidence ledger, data contracts, safety gates, and explicit non-promises are genuinely valuable.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers expecting a live cross-platform control panel: the capability manifest contains export-read operations only, with every v2 account-mutation capability disabled.

reviews.name: ASu-skills
reviews.verdict: Use ASu-skills if you are a Chinese-speaking Codex user who wants one opinionated path from open-source evidence to a finished resume and application tracker.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users, because the supplied documentation and examples are in Chinese Anyone wanting a conventional standalone app, because this is a Codex plugin bundle Teams that require versioned, stable releases, because no release is listed Applicants hoping AI will supply…

reviews.name: claudish-to-english
reviews.verdict: Use it if Claude Code's wording regularly slows you down and you already run Ollama or have a suitable API account.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs guaranteed faithful wording, because another model performs the rewrite Users who want a zero-configuration plugin, especially on Windows People with limited memory or no interest in running a local model or paying API fees Production workflows that…

reviews.name: colleague-skill
reviews.verdict: dot-skill is an inventive, well-presented method for producing richer character instructions than a few adjectives in a prompt.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that cannot obtain informed consent for employee-message collection: the README supports Slack and Feishu API collection, while the project offers no visible consent or retention policy in its main notes.

reviews.name: awesome-deepseek-agent
reviews.verdict: Awesome DeepSeek Agent is a useful first stop if your exact client appears in its table, especially because the guides are short and bilingual.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for an agent runtime or installable library: the repository contains Markdown guides and screenshots, not application code.

reviews.name: skill-up
reviews.verdict: Skill Up is the most focused option here for teams treating Agent Skills as software that deserves repeatable tests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose main problem is skill discovery or routing: issue #166 says positive and negative routing evaluation is still a proposed capability.

reviews.name: claude-squad
reviews.verdict: Claude Squad gives parallel coding agents the missing control room: isolation, live previews, diff review, and quick session switching.
reviews.skip_if: Native Windows users expecting the published binary's main workflow to work: issue 275 says session creation fails because the PTY dependency does not support Windows.

reviews.name: Switchyard
reviews.verdict: Switchyard is an exciting test bench for routing coding-agent traffic across open and hosted models, especially if Rust and protocol translation are central requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require stable APIs or configuration: the README explicitly calls Switchyard pre-alpha, says major changes are expected before 1.0, and warns against production use.

reviews.name: ds4
reviews.verdict: DwarfStar is a brilliant, opinionated take on local inference for the high-end enthusiast.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for a simple, one-click way to run various open-source models.

reviews.name: OpenBot
reviews.verdict: OpenBot has one of the more convincing designs for giving agents real access without treating trust as a prompt-writing exercise.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive production teams that need a settled release today: the README labels OpenBot alpha, and an open issue shows that an allowed agent URL can redirect to an address the initial safety check would refuse.

reviews.name: aegis-vault
reviews.verdict: Aegis Vault is an appealing young project for a narrow audience: technically confident individuals who want typed developer secrets in a fully local vault.
reviews.skip_if: Families and teams that need sharing, permissions, or managed recovery Anyone who expects automatic multi-device sync or browser-wide autofill Users who are uncomfortable running a remote install script from a terminal People who need a long-established security track record or…

reviews.name: buzz
reviews.verdict: Our Buzz checkout exceeded 1 million source lines, and the pnpm install added 611 packages and 445 MB, yet the root package exposed no build or test target for our harness to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Teams replacing Slack, GitHub, or incident tooling this quarter: the README labels Buzz unfinished and lists workflow approvals, mobile clients, and huddle lifecycle work as still being wired up.

reviews.name: pipeshub-ai
reviews.verdict: PipesHub is a serious shortcut for teams that would otherwise build connectors, permission filtering, citations, retrieval, and agent actions themselves.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams seeking a lightweight notes chatbot: the installer recommends 15 GB of host RAM on Linux, 8 GB for Docker Desktop, and 20 GB free disk.

reviews.name: openflight
reviews.verdict: OpenFlight is the strongest open DIY launch-monitor package for makers who want a documented, end-to-end build rather than a loose pile of signal-processing scripts.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers expecting a calibrated commercial appliance: the README warns that OpenFlight is in active development and features can be incomplete, unstable, or change without notice.

reviews.name: Antigravity-Manager
reviews.verdict: Our Antigravity checkout built in 31 seconds, but it installed 817 packages, carried 22 known vulnerabilities, and offered no test target, so this is a personal-lab gateway rather than a service we would trust blindly.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial products that need permissive licensing: the repository uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which limits licensed use to noncommercial purposes and requires ShareAlike for adaptations.

reviews.name: sglang-omni
reviews.verdict: SGLang-Omni is one of the more ambitious open serving layers for modern speech and multimodal pipelines, and its architecture addresses work that ordinary LLM servers do not.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only teams or Mac users: the documented main path targets NVIDIA CUDA, while Intel XPU support is explicitly experimental and limited to three model families.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 4,673 packages and 3,958 MB, passed its test target in 224 seconds, then failed the build because `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was missing, so Cal.diy is testable but configuration-heavy even before deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses or production services: the README strictly recommends Cal.diy for personal, non-production use and directs commercial users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: Pumpkin
reviews.verdict: Pumpkin is a technically exciting server rewrite and a good place to contribute, test protocol behavior, or prototype a future low-overhead network.
reviews.skip_if: Public survival servers that require vanilla correctness today, because the project says it is under heavy development and has no 1.0 release Bukkit, Spigot, or Paper servers that depend on existing Java plugins, because those JAR files cannot run directly…

reviews.name: centaur
reviews.verdict: Centaur is one of the more convincing blueprints for turning personal coding agents into a governed team service.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a bot they can start with Docker Compose: even the local quickstart requires Kubernetes, kubectl, Helm, Docker, several secrets, 1Password integration, and a Slack app.

reviews.name: open-tv
reviews.verdict: Fred TV is an appealing IPTV client for people who already trust their provider and want speed, recording, and a clean remote-controlled interface without running a full media center.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting channels or subscriptions to be included: the README only imports a source you provide, so Fred TV is a player rather than a content service.

reviews.name: check-if-email-exists
reviews.verdict: check-if-email-exists is a serious open-source option when you understand that mailbox verification is probabilistic and operationally awkward.
reviews.skip_if: Proprietary commercial products expecting permissive open-source terms: the README requires a commercial license unless the application is compatible with AGPL-3.0.

reviews.name: AppFlowy
reviews.verdict: AppFlowy is worth a serious trial if Notion's hosted data model is the reason you want to leave and your workflow fits documents, boards, and structured tables.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot accept document-saving risk during migration: release 0.13.2 fixed writes being lost with several tabs open, while current reports describe disappearing card text and unsaved kanban changes.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 4,673 packages into 3,958 MB, passed the tests, and then failed the build because `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was unset, so Cal.diy is a serious self-hosting commitment rather than a quick calendar widget.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses seeking a supported production deployment: the README strictly recommends Cal.diy for personal, non-production use and points commercial users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: workout-guide
reviews.verdict: Our checkout built in 11 seconds and all five Vitest tests passed, so Workout Guide is a credible starting point for adding static exercise art without inventing a catalog.
reviews.skip_if: Products that need coaching, rep counting, timers, workout planning, or user progress: the project supplies exercise metadata and images, not a training engine.

reviews.name: edit
reviews.verdict: Use FMHY when you want a maintained map of free online resources and accept that many destinations are third-party sites requiring your own judgment.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors adding paid or trial-only services, coding libraries, Linux distributions, or multiplayer cheats: the contribution guide explicitly rejects those categories or directs readers elsewhere.

reviews.name: Amagine3D
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 14 seconds, but 5 of 32 tests failed, so Amagine3D is not ready for uncritical production adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require a stable tagged release and a fully passing test suite Beginners expecting a one-command appliance with no Node.js or CAD-runtime knowledge Mechanical engineers who need certified tolerances, simulation, or manufacturing sign-off Users who want a mature…

reviews.name: northcinder
reviews.verdict: Our NorthCinder run passed 183 protocol tests but the 9-second workspace test command still failed in the site package, while the build stopped on Node 20.20.2.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting dependable autonomous research today: the README says no host and model combination is qualified for routine research use.

reviews.name: Open-Generative-AI
reviews.verdict: Open Generative AI is appealing as a broad creative front end, especially if you already want MuAPI and prefer a desktop-style workspace.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who read self-hosted as fully local: the README says the main catalog calls MuAPI, while local inference is desktop-only and covers a smaller set of models.

reviews.name: nakama
reviews.verdict: Our Nakama build passed in 37 seconds, but the 466-second test run ended with 3 database failures and 8 server failures, so this active v0.4.3 project still needs operator scrutiny.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that let untrusted users install custom tools: critical issue #447 says JavaScript handlers run inside the server process and Python receives the full server environment.

reviews.name: OpenMausBot
reviews.verdict: OpenMausBot is one of the more coherent attempts to make multiple local agents feel manageable rather than merely powerful.
reviews.skip_if: Nontechnical users expecting a self-contained assistant, because the core engines must already be installed and authenticated Teams needing a proven, centrally administered production platform with a long release history Anyone uncomfortable granting local agents access to shell commands, files, or…

reviews.name: LingChat
reviews.verdict: LingChat is one of the most imaginative open companion interfaces, but version 0.5 expanded its power faster than its security boundary.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who plans to enable agent command execution or install untrusted plugins on a valuable machine: issue 614 documents command, approval, plugin, LAN-sync, and secret-storage weaknesses in v0.5.0, while the proposed hardening patch is unmerged and uncompiled.

reviews.name: nofx
reviews.verdict: NOFX is an ambitious and thoughtfully constrained experiment, not a system we would trust with meaningful unattended capital.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot lose the full account balance: the project's disclaimer says the experimental software may behave unpredictably and losses can exceed the initial deposit.

reviews.name: compozy
reviews.verdict: Our CompozyOS build stopped after 18 seconds at Go module parsing, and the current v0.3 line is still beta, so production teams should trial it beside existing automation before handing it unattended work.
reviews.skip_if: Existing v0.2 users who need an in-place upgrade: the README says v0.3 does not revive the old `tasks run` pipeline and requires the migration guide.

reviews.name: modly
reviews.verdict: Modly is one of the friendlier ways to explore several local image-to-3D models without living at a Python prompt, and its workflow and automation ideas are promising.
reviews.skip_if: AMD GPU owners who need a supported accelerated path today: an open request says AMD hardware is not supported, while the ROCm detection work remains an unmerged pull request.

reviews.name: meetily
reviews.verdict: Meetily is worth trying for an individual who wants local meeting transcription and has a supported desktop, especially because the free code is inspectable and the packaged start is approachable.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the open Community Edition to provide shared self-hosted deployment: the README places team deployment in Meetily Pro, which it says uses a different codebase.

reviews.name: VibeVoice
reviews.verdict: VibeVoice is worth testing for long meetings where one pass should produce words, timestamps, and speaker turns, or for research on low-latency English speech.
reviews.skip_if: Production buyers seeking Microsoft's endorsement for deployment: the README says commercial and real-world use needs further testing and development.

reviews.name: semantica
reviews.verdict: Semantica is a serious, heavyweight tool for solving the critical problem of AI accountability in high-stakes environments.
reviews.skip_if: Hobbyists or developers building simple chatbots where auditability is not a concern.

reviews.name: claude-task-master
reviews.verdict: Taskmaster is an ambitious and powerful tool for structuring AI-driven development, especially for those embedded in the Cursor ecosystem.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who are just starting with AI code assistants; the setup and concepts can be overwhelming.

reviews.name: ccg-workflow
reviews.verdict: CCG-Workflow is an ambitious and brilliantly architected tool that offers a glimpse into the future of AI-driven software development.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who are not comfortable with command-line interfaces or the concepts of multi-agent AI systems.

reviews.name: plandex
reviews.verdict: Plandex is a conceptually brilliant AI coding agent, especially for developers wrestling with massive codebases.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners or developers who strongly prefer a graphical user interface; Plandex is a power-user tool for the terminal.

reviews.name: Vane
reviews.verdict: Our Vane install took 274 seconds, pulled 1,051 packages, and occupied 2,039 MB, while the repository offered no test target, so the polished Docker pitch hides a heavy and weakly verified code path.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose it directly to the public internet: the README lists authentication as an upcoming feature, and issue 1180 reports API keys exposed to client-side code.

reviews.name: Prompt-Engineering-Guide
reviews.verdict: Prompt Engineering Guide is still a good free index for learning the vocabulary and finding original papers.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking current provider API documentation: the guide is organized by concepts and papers, while model behavior and endpoints change faster than this repository lands updates.

reviews.name: OpenMontage
reviews.verdict: OpenMontage is unusually inspectable for an agent-led video system: its manifests, checkpoints, approvals, budgets, and render artifacts live in the project instead of disappearing behind a chat session.
reviews.skip_if: Nontechnical editors expecting a normal timeline application: the main interface is an AI coding assistant working through files and commands.

reviews.name: RuView
reviews.verdict: RuView is fascinating as an RF sensing laboratory and unusually candid in parts of its README about weak or synthetic evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Care providers or safety teams seeking a certified monitor: the README calls the health, fall, and emergency uses research prototypes rather than medical or safety-certified systems.

reviews.name: mcp
reviews.verdict: AWSLabs MCP is a powerful and pioneering toolkit for integrating deep AWS knowledge into AI development workflows, but it has been officially superseded.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone building production-grade, business-critical AI agents.

reviews.name: xiaozhi-esp32-server
reviews.verdict: Xiaozhi is an incredibly powerful and feature-rich backend for DIY voice assistants on ESP32 hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners without experience in both hardware (ESP32) and server deployment (Docker, source code).

reviews.name: ai-engineering-hub
reviews.verdict: Our measured researcher installed 33 packages in 30 seconds and built in 11 seconds, but it exposed no test target and the repository has 0 CI workflows.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for one supported production platform: the repository is a gallery of independent projects with separate dependencies and operating assumptions.

reviews.name: OmniRoute
reviews.verdict: OmniRoute is compelling for an individual power user who already pays for several AI products and wants one local control panel.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams unwilling to put provider keys, OAuth sessions, browser-cookie integrations, and local proxy behavior in one application: the README documents all of these connection styles.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: emilkowalski/skills is a clever and timely project that packages high-level design expertise into a format AI agents can understand.
reviews.skip_if: Developers not using AI or LLM-based agents for coding; the project's value is entirely in guiding these agents.

reviews.name: zapret-discord-youtube
reviews.verdict: Our 2026-08-26 Debian lab with 3 CPUs and 8 GB of RAM could not run this Windows Batch and WinDivert bundle, so no independent install or test result exists.
reviews.skip_if: Linux, macOS, Android, or iOS users: the documented package is built around Windows Batch files, services, `netsh`, and the WinDivert driver.

reviews.name: backlink_skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run backlink_skills because it found no supported executable ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so this review cannot offer an independent install or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a one-click backlink bot: the README explicitly rejects link spam, ranking manipulation, verification bypass, invented profiles, paid links, and forced reciprocal links.

reviews.name: macos-harness
reviews.verdict: Our Debian run built macOS Harness in 7 seconds, then passed 10 of 26 tests because the remaining 16 required unavailable macOS ApplicationServices bindings.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the README labels the project macOS-only, and 16 tests failed in our Debian sandbox because ApplicationServices bindings were unavailable.

reviews.name: gastown
reviews.verdict: Gas Town tackles the coordination problems that appear once terminal agents outnumber the operator's attention, and its persistent ledger is more useful than another grid of tmux panes.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers running one or two agents: the Mayor, rigs, polecats, convoys, witnesses, and refineries add more machinery than a small workflow needs.

reviews.name: mcp-server
reviews.verdict: SV Number MCP Server is a focused, unusually well-explained bridge between an agent and a paid verification-number API.
reviews.skip_if: Banking, payment, or government-account workflows: the README explicitly says the numbers are not meant for those services.

reviews.name: eve-software-factory-template
reviews.verdict: Foreman is one of the more coherent examples of a multi-agent software pipeline because each stage has a defined job and the final product is a draft pull request, not an automatic merge.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a provider-neutral or fully local factory: the sandbox configuration pins Vercel Sandbox even for local development, which requires a linked and authenticated Vercel project.

reviews.name: phone-harness
reviews.verdict: Phone Harness is the most interesting option here for exploratory, agent-driven work on a real phone, especially when the task cannot be moved to a web API.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the package declares macOS as its environment, installs PyObjC frameworks, and the setup guide uses Mac-specific iPhone Mirroring and Homebrew paths.

reviews.name: youtube-automation-agent
reviews.verdict: YouTube Automation Agent is an unusually approachable demonstration of a complete AI-to-YouTube pipeline, but it is not ready for unattended public publishing.
reviews.skip_if: Creators who need generated images to appear reliably in current slideshow output: open pull request 19 reproduces a master-branch bug that discards every local image and renders only the gradient background.

reviews.name: automatisch
reviews.verdict: Automatisch is a compelling choice if data sovereignty is your non-negotiable top priority.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need the largest possible library of pre-built app integrations; established players like Zapier have a massive head start.

reviews.name: Dalaran
reviews.verdict: Dalaran has an unusually focused robotics design, and its ROS conventions, costmap handling, diagnostics, and portable bundles address real daily annoyances.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require a long stability record, because the repository is only days old and has no listed release Users wanting a general business dashboard or metrics platform, because Dalaran is narrowly shaped around robotics data Teams that need…

reviews.name: quant-mind
reviews.verdict: QuantMind is worth studying if your immediate job is turning papers or PR Newswire into inspectable financial knowledge, especially with an agent editing the pipeline.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need SEC filings or prediction-market ingestion today: the README lists both as directions that have not shipped.

reviews.name: ChinaTextbook
reviews.verdict: ChinaTextbook is an immensely popular and valuable archive of Chinese educational materials, but it's best viewed as a dormant library, not an active project.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot read Mandarin, as the entire project and all its contents are in Chinese.

reviews.name: Wake
reviews.verdict: Our build failed after 896 seconds because the linker could not find `-lxkbcommon-x11`.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs team sharing, cloud sync, or remote access Windows and Linux users who require polished, proven desktop integration today Users of Windsurf, Trae, Amp, Factory, or Warp, whose sessions are not supported People unwilling to bypass Gatekeeper or…

reviews.name: x64dbg-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Version 1.1 gives an MCP client 84 debugger tools over unencrypted HTTP, so x64dbg-MCP Server should be treated like a remote code-and-memory control plane, not a convenience plugin.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone debugging software without explicit authorization: the plugin can execute commands, write process memory, dump modules, and manipulate a live target.

reviews.name: andrej-karpathy-skills
reviews.verdict: Use andrej-karpathy-skills if your main complaint is that Claude Code guesses too much, edits too broadly, or turns small jobs into large designs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need measured proof that the rules improve coding outcomes: the tested commit contains examples, while a benchmark and runner remain in an open pull request.

reviews.name: dsh-gitbash-preset
reviews.verdict: Use it if DeepSeek Harness minimal mode is already part of your Windows workflow and its broken bash support is the exact obstacle.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users, because the plugin solves a Windows-specific failure Anyone needing a persistent shell, since cd and export state do not survive calls Locked-down environments that cannot approve full access for Git Bash Beginners seeking English-first documentation or…

reviews.name: CVE-2026-9830
reviews.verdict: Use this only when your exact job is to validate CVE-2026-9830 on a BookingPress Pro installation you are authorized to assess.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone scanning public or third-party sites without written permission Teams seeking a general WordPress vulnerability scanner, since this targets one reported issue Beginners who are not prepared to protect or delete sensitive JSON output Production operators who want a supported,…

reviews.name: anti-slop
reviews.verdict: anti-slop is worth studying if weak TypeScript boundaries and AI-generated type laundering keep surviving ordinary lint checks.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that depend heavily on Jest or Vitest module mocks: `no-module-mocking` rejects `jest.mock` and `vi.mock` rather than accommodating that testing style.

reviews.name: mxc
reviews.verdict: Our MXC run installed 222 packages, then both build and test commands stopped because `windows-future` could not find `windows_threading::submit`, so the current source checkout is a research target rather than a drop-in containment layer.
reviews.skip_if: Production systems that need MXC itself to protect hosts or secrets: the README says current profiles are not security boundaries and generated policies have known overly permissive cases.

reviews.name: pr-af
reviews.verdict: PR-AF has a thoughtful architecture and one of the better evidence packages behind an open AI reviewer, but it is still an early engineering project rather than a dependable merge gate.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require an unambiguous open-source grant before evaluation: the README badge and package metadata say Apache 2.0, but the repository has no `LICENSE` file and GitHub detects no license.

reviews.name: manim
reviews.verdict: ManimGL is the right choice when you want the engine and interactive habits closest to current 3Blue1Brown production.
reviews.skip_if: Most first-time Manim users: this repository's README says Manim Community aims to be more stable, better tested, more responsive to contributions, and friendlier to start with.

reviews.name: Dopamine
reviews.verdict: Dopamine is the leading option to try when its exact hardware and iOS matrix matches your device and you want a modern rootless jailbreak.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone outside the published chip and iOS combinations: the README says version-support issues will be deleted without a response, so unsupported devices are not an experimental target.

reviews.name: Impactor
reviews.verdict: Impactor is a capable choice for users who need one desktop tool for signing, installing, pairing, and SideStore-related files across three operating systems.
reviews.skip_if: People unwilling to enter an Apple Account into a third-party application: Impactor uses it to request certificates, profiles, and device registration from Apple.

reviews.name: claude-code-security-review
reviews.verdict: Claude Code Security Review is a promising advisory reviewer, especially for business-logic and context-dependent mistakes that rule scanners may miss.
reviews.skip_if: Public repositories that automatically run untrusted contributor code: the README explicitly says the action is not hardened against prompt injection and recommends maintainer approval for every external contributor.

reviews.name: Lighthouse
reviews.verdict: Lighthouse is an exciting and ambitious project that offers a glimpse into the future of retro gaming.
reviews.skip_if: Casual retro gamers who just want to play a variety of N64 games; a general-purpose emulator like Project64 is a much simpler choice.

reviews.name: localstack
reviews.verdict: LocalStack remains useful for local AWS integration work, but this archived repository is no longer the product I would adopt.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking an actively maintained open-source upstream: this repository is archived and read-only, with future work consolidated into a unified image.

reviews.name: sam
reviews.verdict: SAM solves a problem that becomes real once agents and MCP servers span several networks: identity, discovery, and remote calls cannot remain a pile of tunnels and public URLs.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require a supported Google product: the README explicitly says SAM is not officially supported by Google and is ineligible for Google's open-source vulnerability rewards program.

reviews.name: book-to-skill
reviews.verdict: Use book-to-skill as an interesting local workflow, not yet as trusted knowledge infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a polished hosted app with account sync and support People working mainly with scanned PDFs, because OCR must happen first Teams that need verbatim, citation-grade retrieval from source pages Users unwilling to install format-specific tools or inspect generated…

reviews.name: dsh-anchored-standard
reviews.verdict: dsh-anchored-standard is valuable as an unusually well-documented research artifact, not as a proven upgrade every DeepSeek Harness user should install.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need an actively developed production dependency: the maintainer says active development stopped on 2026-08-17 and only feasible maintenance fixes remain.

reviews.name: dsh-routing-suite
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-routing-suite build stopped after 6 seconds because it could not find the required DSH checkout, even though its 37-package npm install and audit completed cleanly.
reviews.skip_if: Users of general chat APIs, Claude Code, or other agents without DeepSeek Harness: the injector depends on DSH packages, profiles, services, and event hooks.

reviews.name: defending-code-reference-harness
reviews.verdict: Use this repository as an architectural reference and a demanding workshop, not as your security product.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a supported scanner or dependable upstream fixes: the README says the repository is not maintained and does not accept contributions.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness
reviews.verdict: DeepSeek Harness is technically interesting and unusually transparent about its internal contracts, but it is still a developer preview with no latest GitHub release and a failing clean test run.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams requiring stable compatibility: the README labels the project a developer preview and explicitly warns of breaking changes.

reviews.name: corsair
reviews.verdict: Corsair has the right central idea: an agent should receive narrow tools and governed actions, not a bag of reusable credentials.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a zero-infrastructure connector: the quick start requires a database, four tables, a key-encryption key, Hub credentials, and an application route.

reviews.name: needle
reviews.verdict: Needle is one of the most interesting options for a narrow class of offline agents where memory use matters more than broad language ability.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a general chat assistant: the README says Needle solves tasks as function calls, returns an empty call for unsupported requests, and has no free-text fallback for off-topic input.

reviews.name: airllm
reviews.verdict: Our AirLLM install took 120 seconds and its build took 16 seconds, but the repo gave us no test target, so it is best treated as an experiment for running oversized models rather than a proven serving layer.
reviews.skip_if: Teams serving latency-sensitive chat or high-throughput APIs: AirLLM streams weights from disk, and its own FAQ identifies disk loading as the bottleneck.

reviews.name: continue
reviews.verdict: Our Continue install took 16 seconds and reported 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but the maintainers now call 2.0.0 the final release and the repository read-only.
reviews.skip_if: Teams choosing a newly maintained coding assistant: the README says this repository is no longer actively maintained and calls 2.0.0 the final release.

reviews.name: nasiko
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 695 packages in 26 seconds, but Nasiko's server failed to compile in both the 279-second build and 111-second test run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with agents on A2A 0.2.x or 0.3.0: the README says Nasiko hardcodes A2A 1.0 and rejects older protocol versions.

reviews.name: WeChat-AI
reviews.verdict: WeChat-AI is an unusually complete personal-WeChat companion stack, but it is best treated as an ambitious early project, not settled infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Companies, consultants, or paid hosting providers: the README restricts use to personal and noncommercial work, and the Commons Clause forbids selling hosting, support, or a product whose value substantially comes from the software.

reviews.name: colibri
reviews.verdict: Colibrì is worth trying if its research question is your problem: how to run enormous sparse models without requiring all weights to live in expensive memory.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a polished, supported production service with an SLA Beginners who want a one-command local chat app and a small download Teams that need predictable latency across workloads without extensive testing Users who assume fitting a model through storage…

reviews.name: Crucix
reviews.verdict: Crucix is exciting as a local OSINT experiment and unsafe as a trusted intelligence product in its current default branch.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose the current dashboard to untrusted users: issue 134 documents stored cross-site scripting paths from feed and LLM text, and its fix remains an open pull request.

reviews.name: remote.futrx
reviews.verdict: Remote is one of the more coherent self-hosted answers to the mess of agent terminals, browser tabs, previews, and persistent sessions.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need strong isolation between invited users: the documented limitations say any invited user can reach any project's code-server IDE, and project members can read and change that project's plaintext secrets.

reviews.name: rustfs
reviews.verdict: Our RustFS build and test commands each spent 900 seconds compiling without finishing, while the README still marks distributed mode under testing, so it is an evaluation candidate rather than a safe drop-in storage replacement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams replacing proven storage without a long acceptance test: the README labels distributed mode and lifecycle management as under testing.

reviews.name: macro
reviews.verdict: Macro is one of the more coherent attempts to make a team's work legible to both people and agents, and its bidirectional links are a better foundation than another set of shallow integrations.
reviews.skip_if: Outlook or custom IMAP and SMTP teams: the getting-started guide says Macro currently syncs Gmail and Google Workspace, while other mail support is only planned.

reviews.name: mapcn
reviews.verdict: mapcn is a good shortcut for a shadcn-style dashboard that needs a polished map and accepts source ownership.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams expecting the default tiles to be free: the README says commercial use of the included CARTO basemaps requires a CARTO Enterprise license.

reviews.name: TizenTube
reviews.verdict: TizenTube is the best first project to try if you own a recent Samsung TV and already accept the friction of sideloaded Tizen software.
reviews.skip_if: Android or Google TV owners: the README directs those users to the separate TizenTube Cobalt project.

reviews.name: Viscose-carousel
reviews.verdict: Viscose Carousel is excellent source material and an unusually well-explained WebGL experiment, but it is not a drop-in portfolio.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs an accessible carousel out of the box: the README lists no keyboard controls and no reduced-motion path among the known gaps.

reviews.name: dsh-deep-whale
reviews.verdict: Use dsh-deep-whale if you already have the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, like its specific character art, and are certain your use is noncommercial.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial deployments, because the skins prohibit commercial use Teams needing a neutral, workplace-oriented interface Users who do not already run a compatible DeepSeek Harness Web GUI Anyone requiring a stable release channel, versioned upgrades, or English documentation

reviews.name: servo
reviews.verdict: Our Servo tooling install took 500 seconds and 294 MB, then the build exited in 16 seconds and pytest produced 69 setup or collection errors, so this checkout is research infrastructure rather than a drop-in webview.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a daily browser with Chrome, Firefox, or Safari compatibility: Servo's own README calls it a prototype engine.

reviews.name: octo-web
reviews.verdict: OCTO Web looks like a serious, rapidly developed workplace client, but evaluating it apart from the rest of OCTO is misleading.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a standalone chat server, because this repository is only a client and expects octo-server Small self-hosters wanting one-container setup, because major features span a nine-repository ecosystem Operators who need long-term support for older releases, because the security policy…

reviews.name: ladybird
reviews.verdict: Ladybird is worth following, testing, and reading if browser engines are your field.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a daily browser today: the README labels Ladybird pre-alpha and suitable only for developers.

reviews.name: apex-inference-chip
reviews.verdict: Our 8-second Python-side build succeeded with 35 packages, but the harness found no test target and did not reproduce the FPGA claims.
reviews.skip_if: Teams shopping for a production inference server or purchasable chip: the README calls APEX pre-silicon and limits the repository to one tile.

reviews.name: SQLBot
reviews.verdict: SQLBot is worth a controlled pilot for Chinese-speaking teams that want a packaged conversational BI product with permissions, charts, embedding, and MCP access.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require an unmodified OSI-standard license: the FIT2CLOUD license adds a ban on replacing or changing SQLBot branding and copyright information.

reviews.name: cumora
reviews.verdict: Cumora is one of the more convincing attempts to turn coding agents into visible teammates instead of isolated chat boxes.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users relying on the documented BYOA path today: open issues report that the published npm package fails to spawn npm-installed agent CLIs and that Windows has no supported background service installer.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness-studio
reviews.verdict: DeepSeek Harness Studio is unusually ambitious for such a young repository, and its plugin discovery, preset installation, and desktop supervision story is more concrete than a typical mockup-heavy launch.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that need a stable, versioned release line, because the available downloads are labeled preview release candidates Linux desktop users, because only macOS arm64 and Windows x64 packages are advertised People expecting every roadmap feature today, because Git, multi-agent…

reviews.name: oil-motion
reviews.verdict: Oil Motion is a thoughtful production recipe for a difficult visual niche, and its budgeting, keying, runtime, and QA rules are far more useful than a folder of prompts.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams that need to audit or modify the production procedure: the English README is useful, but `SKILL.md` and all nine reference guides are Chinese, and the pull request translating those guides is still open.

reviews.name: h3.c
reviews.verdict: Use h3.c if you have a high-memory Apple Silicon machine and specifically want to study or run MiniMax-H3 through a transparent native implementation.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, NVIDIA, or Intel Mac users, because this implementation targets Apple Silicon and Metal Beginners expecting a packaged app, hosted service, or one-click installer Production teams that require versioned releases, compatibility guarantees, and a stable public API Users without…

reviews.name: video-use
reviews.verdict: video-use is a sharp demonstration of how a coding agent can make useful editing decisions without consuming every video frame.
reviews.skip_if: Editors who need a visual timeline, manual trimming, or frame-by-frame control: the project deliberately offers no menus and expects all direction through an agent.

reviews.name: exo
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 5 seconds and pip-audit found 0 vulnerabilities, but pytest ran 0 tests because `exo_tools` was missing, and the exact measured commit has an open report of remotely reachable data deletion through its unauthenticated API.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users expecting GPU inference today: the README says Linux currently runs on CPU and GPU support is under development.

reviews.name: everyone-can-use-english
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 2,681 packages and used 2,624 MB, while the lab found no generic build or test target, so contributors inherit much more uncertainty than hosted users.
reviews.skip_if: English-speaking users who need complete documentation in English: the root README and learning guides are Chinese, and issue #1409 asks for basic product instructions even in Chinese.

reviews.name: deepwiki-rs
reviews.verdict: Litho is worth a controlled trial when you need orientation material from a codebase and will treat the result as a draft.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a cheap, predictable run on a large monorepo: one open report describes spending more than $100 while analyzing 1,697 files before a 504 stopped generation.

reviews.name: MiroFish
reviews.verdict: MiroFish is best treated as a scenario generator with an engaging interface, not a machine for learning what will happen.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone making financial, political, safety, or policy decisions from a claimed forecast: the project does not establish scientific calibration, causal validity, or prediction confidence.

reviews.name: go-cursor-help
reviews.verdict: This tool is a brutally simple and effective solution for resetting Cursor's trial, but it's a solution frozen in time.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone in a professional or corporate environment, as using this tool likely violates Cursor's terms of service and company policies.

reviews.name: onlook
reviews.verdict: Onlook is a fascinating and ambitious glimpse into the future of web development, where AI and direct visual manipulation eliminate the friction between design and code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that don't use Next.js and Tailwind CSS.

reviews.name: system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools
reviews.verdict: This is less a software project and more a controversial but valuable dataset.
reviews.skip_if: Non-technical users looking for a runnable application or a simple AI tool.

reviews.name: Kronos
reviews.verdict: Kronos is worth testing as a finance-specific research baseline, particularly because three model sizes, inference code, and a fine-tuning example are public under MIT terms.
reviews.skip_if: Traders seeking an automated strategy: the README calls its top-K backtest a simplified demonstration and says real use needs portfolio construction, risk controls, transaction costs, slippage, and market impact.

reviews.name: ruflo
reviews.verdict: Ruflo is interesting for expert Claude Code and Codex users who have already hit the limits of one agent and can audit a large amount of installed machinery.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a small, predictable extension: the full initializer writes `.claude/`, `.claude-flow/`, `CLAUDE.md`, helpers, settings, hooks, a daemon, and an MCP registration.

reviews.name: GenAI_Agents
reviews.verdict: GenAI_Agents is less of an open-source project and more of a freemium educational product.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a production-ready library or framework to import into a project.

reviews.name: UI-TARS-desktop
reviews.verdict: Our UI-TARS-desktop run installed a 1,910 MB workspace and failed 57 of 337 tests, so this is an experimental agent stack to isolate and supervise, not a dependable unattended operator.
reviews.skip_if: Multi-monitor desktop users: the quick start says only single-monitor setups are supported and other layouts may fail.

reviews.name: GitHub520
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 61 packages and built in 7 seconds, but the absence of a test target and 5 pip-audit findings make GitHub520's generator less reassuring than its tiny size suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot read Chinese technical instructions: the README and current issue discussion are Chinese, with no English guide in the repository.

reviews.name: Cybermes
reviews.verdict: Our Cybermes install added 252 packages and the audit found six high-severity advisories, while the repository offered no npm test target, so this is a framework to isolate and inspect before it touches an authorized target.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who expect the framework to make authorization decisions for them: the troubleshooting guide says wildcard dynamic target authorization is enabled by default, and the sample environment sets `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1`.

reviews.name: lanshu-create-ai-presenter-video
reviews.verdict: Our install added 35 packages in 11 seconds and the build passed in 4 seconds, but no test target exercised an actual video job.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the repository itself to generate a presenter: the README requires at least one callable video-generation, voice-generation, and lip-sync capability in the current environment.

reviews.name: tradingview-mcp
reviews.verdict: Use TradingView MCP as a supervised research and Pine development aid, with a pinned Desktop version and backups of every saved script.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a supported TradingView integration: the bridge uses undocumented Electron internals that the README says can break after a Desktop update.

reviews.name: projeto-dados-ia-databricks
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 11 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but the repository supplied no automated test target.
reviews.skip_if: English-only learners: the main README, lesson guides, column names, prompts, slides, and business vocabulary are in Portuguese, with no English guide.

reviews.name: desktop-fly
reviews.verdict: Our 4-second Python-side build succeeded, but no test target ran and the macOS Swift application was outside that sandbox result.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users expecting official support: the README requires macOS 13 or newer, while issues #7 and #8 point to separate community ports.

reviews.name: tickflow-stock-panel
reviews.verdict: TickFlow Stock Panel has an unusually broad A-share workflow for a personal open-source project, but it is not ready to trust without engineering work.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial adopters who need clear permission: the repository declares MIT, while the README also says commercial use is strictly prohibited.

reviews.name: pdf-inspector
reviews.verdict: For its specific niche, fast, local, OCR-free PDF processing, pdf-inspector is a category leader in performance.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing to extract text from scanned documents, photographs, or image-only PDFs.

reviews.name: herdrm
reviews.verdict: herdrm requires macOS 14 or newer, a herdr daemon on each machine, and agent bypass permissions are enabled by default, so adoption should begin on non-sensitive development hosts.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone on Windows, Linux, or macOS 13 and older: the app requires macOS 14 or newer.

reviews.name: dsh-explore
reviews.verdict: Use Deepseek Harness Explore as a focused technical reading resource, not as the foundation of a production system.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a ready-to-deploy agent framework, because this is mainly an explanatory publication Readers who need the full article collection in English, because the articles are stated to be Chinese Buyers who require a stable release, declared license, and production…

reviews.name: nft-public-mint
reviews.verdict: NFT Public Mint Sniper is unusually clear about its narrow job, and its small codebase is a better trust proposition than an opaque minting executable.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone joining an allowlist or first-come, first-served signed stage: the README says those use SeaDrop `mintSigned()` and require an OpenSea-generated wallet signature that this tool cannot obtain.

reviews.name: cordis
reviews.verdict: Our Cordis checkout installed 432 packages with 0 known vulnerabilities, but both build and test stopped within 10 seconds because the npm-created workspace state did not satisfy Yarn 4.14.1.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams wanting a stable public API: the README says Cordis is under active development and may change without notice.

reviews.name: res-downloader
reviews.verdict: res-downloader solves a genuinely awkward problem for people pulling media from Chinese desktop and mobile ecosystems, and its visual filtering is friendlier than a raw proxy log.
reviews.skip_if: Corporate or security-sensitive computers where installing a trusted interception certificate and proxying HTTPS traffic is unacceptable: both steps are required by the README.

reviews.name: nanoGPT
reviews.verdict: Use nanoGPT as a teaching text or a disposable research base when its small surface is the point.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone starting a new Karpathy-style language-model project: the README says nanoGPT is deprecated and points readers to `karpathy/nanochat`.

reviews.name: lean-ctx
reviews.verdict: Our LeanCTX source build succeeded in 402 seconds, but its 223-second test run exited 101 and current issues report broken safety and verbatim-read expectations.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone relying on IDE plan mode as a security boundary: open issue 1500 says `ctx_shell`, `ctx_execute`, and `ctx_patch` remain callable in plan or readonly mode.

reviews.name: anime-find
reviews.verdict: Use anime-find if DeepSeek Harness Web is already your daily interface and its Chinese-language anime sources match how you search; the card-to-resource workflow is unusually well thought through for such a young plugin.
reviews.skip_if: People looking for a standalone anime app; this depends on DeepSeek Harness Web Anyone who needs an English-first setup and troubleshooting experience Users expecting licensed content, guaranteed source uptime, or a turnkey streaming catalog Teams that need a mature, broadly…

reviews.name: computer
reviews.verdict: Cloudflare Computer is an ambitious and exciting preview of what stateful serverless computing could look like.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone building a production system.

reviews.name: autogen
reviews.verdict: Do not start a new project on AutoGen.
reviews.skip_if: Any greenfield project: the README says AutoGen receives no new features and tells new users to start with Microsoft Agent Framework.

reviews.name: walgit
reviews.verdict: Our walgit build ran for 643 seconds before `walgit-server` failed with 3 compiler errors, and tests hit the same compilation boundary after 271 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a GitHub or GitLab replacement with issues, pull requests, CI, and code review: the README scopes walgit to repository serving and browsing.

reviews.name: evolution-api
reviews.verdict: Evolution API makes sense when its unusually wide set of WhatsApp, webhook, queue, CRM, and storage connections would replace glue code you already expect to maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean source build from the measured commit: our build stopped on missing Prisma client exports, including `Contact`, `Message`, `Proxy`, and `Prisma.sql`.

reviews.name: tick-stock-panel
reviews.verdict: Tick Stock Panel is worth trying for a Chinese-reading A-share hobbyist who wants local data and a broad research interface.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README, setup guide, configuration reference, interface examples, and linked manuals are in Chinese, with no English guide listed.

reviews.name: fluxer
reviews.verdict: Our Fluxer checkout installed 1,761 packages, then its 176-second build failed on a missing Rust wasm target and its 77-second test run ended with 2 application test failures.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters who require desktop clients today: the operator guide says the desktop app cannot connect to self-hosted instances yet.

reviews.name: substrate
reviews.verdict: Agent Substrate is an unusually ambitious and technically coherent research project for a real emerging problem: keeping vast fleets of idle, stateful agents affordable.
reviews.skip_if: Production workloads, because the README explicitly says the project is not ready and APIs are almost guaranteed to change Multi-tenant systems requiring a proven security boundary, because the June 2026 threat model says the current product has little to no…

reviews.name: JavBoss
reviews.verdict: JavBoss is a promising specialist library for Chinese-speaking collectors, with a notably cohesive path from filename recognition to metadata, filtering, screenshots, and playback.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: there is no English documentation, and open issue #186 reports that the English language selection disappeared after upgrading to 1.9.0.

reviews.name: TencentDB-Agent-Memory
reviews.verdict: Our MemoryCore install consumed 966 MB, its build and tests both failed, and npm audit found 24 vulnerabilities, so v2.0.1 needs a guarded trial rather than immediate production trust.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers seeking a tiny memory library: our MemoryCore install pulled 541 packages and occupied 966 MB before the other services were running.

reviews.name: scroll-craft
reviews.verdict: The lab found JavaScript but no supported executable target or Dockerfile, so scrollcraft has no independent build or test result on our page.
reviews.skip_if: Developers outside Claude Code who want a documented first-class install path: the README installs it through Claude Code's plugin marketplace.

reviews.name: router
reviews.verdict: speedy-router is an unusually clear and testable performance experiment, but it is still a very young compatibility implementation, not a routine drop-in dependency.
reviews.skip_if: React 18 or Node 22 projects, because those versions are intentionally unsupported Conservative production teams that need years of adoption history and a large support community Apps expecting every TanStack Router edge case to be proven compatible already Teams seeking…

reviews.name: youtube-music
reviews.verdict: This is an appealingly focused experiment, but it is too new and too lightly documented for an unconditional recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a proven, long-supported daily music player macOS or Linux users, since the documented download is a Windows EXE Security-sensitive users unwilling to run an executable from a password-protected ZIP People who need offline downloads, which the project…

reviews.name: biosecurity-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Biosecurity Agent run installed 576 packages, used 686 MB, and passed all 83 tests, so version 0.1.2 is more than a terminal mockup.
reviews.skip_if: Clinicians or patients seeking diagnosis or treatment: the README explicitly says the project is not for clinical diagnosis, and the safety code rejects some diagnostic and dosage language.

reviews.name: watermark-remover
reviews.verdict: Our build passed in 7 seconds, but the test run failed after 80 seconds because installer subprocesses could not open `install_skill.py`, so the deterministic cleaners look useful while this repository's distribution path is not yet trustworthy.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone trying to pass AI-assisted work off as human-written: the project's ethics guide rejects that use, and removed marks do not change authorship.

reviews.name: WhatDreamsCost-ComfyUI
reviews.verdict: LTX Director is an ambitious and genuinely useful interface for creators already committed to LTX inside ComfyUI.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting a self-contained editor: the README requires current ComfyUI-LTXVideo and KJNodes installations, while the GGUF example adds ComfyUI-GGUF and none are pinned in package metadata.

reviews.name: cwc-workshops
reviews.verdict: Use cwc-workshops as a pattern library and guided lab, especially if you already have Managed Agents access and want to see several platform features connected end to end.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a maintained production starter: the root README and individual workshops explicitly say they are not maintained and do not accept contributions.

reviews.name: OSWorld
reviews.verdict: OSWorld is a powerful and necessary tool for the serious work of evaluating computer-operating AI agents.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for a simple automation tool; this is a complex research framework, not a point-and-click macro recorder.

reviews.name: gpt_nerver
reviews.verdict: Treat gpt_nerver as an unusually detailed but very young reference implementation, not a turnkey operations product.
reviews.skip_if: Ordinary ChatGPT Plus subscribers, because this is an operations console rather than a subscription client Anyone expecting a clone-and-run bulk automation tool, because key paths require private or paid services Teams needing a supported production product, stable releases, or a…

reviews.name: ambient-context
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 79 packages in 5 seconds, built in 6 seconds, and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but no automated test target ran.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac, Windows, Linux, or older macOS users: the README requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple Silicon.

reviews.name: babua-dsa-patterns-course
reviews.verdict: Use Babua DSA Patterns Course if Hindi instruction and a fixed daily sequence help you keep practicing.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need English spoken instruction: the README says the explanations are in Hindi, although the main written pages are in English.

reviews.name: paper
reviews.verdict: Read this paper if you are designing a serious plugin host or self-modifying agent runtime, because it gives unusually precise names and rules to problems that are often handled with restart hooks.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for an installable library in this repository: it contains only a README and PDF, while the implementation lives separately in `cordiverse/cordis`.

reviews.name: PLFM_RADAR
reviews.verdict: AERIS-10 is an unusually open and ambitious radar engineering reference, but it is not yet a dependable recipe for obtaining the headline ranges.
reviews.skip_if: Software-only makers looking for a weekend radar kit: the README requires PCB assembly, FPGA tooling, and radar knowledge, and says no standalone assembly guide is tracked.

reviews.name: blitz
reviews.verdict: Blitz is exciting infrastructure work with a thoughtful architecture and unusually transparent compatibility tracking.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams, because the maintainers explicitly say Blitz is pre-alpha and should not yet be used to build apps Products needing full browser compatibility, because JavaScript, storage, WebRTC, and many HTML controls are intentionally absent or unfinished Users enabling the…

reviews.name: swarm-forge
reviews.verdict: SwarmForge is a brilliantly unconventional tool for developers who live in the terminal.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners unfamiliar with `tmux`, shell scripting, or advanced git concepts like worktrees.

reviews.name: reverse-skill
reviews.verdict: reverse-skill is a brilliant and wildly ambitious attempt to solve a real problem: AI agents are powerful but lack strategic, domain-specific knowledge for complex security tasks.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners in cybersecurity.

reviews.name: SpiderPanel
reviews.verdict: Our SpiderPanel install pulled 66 packages and pip-audit found 34 known vulnerabilities, while the repository supplied no test target or CI workflow, so it is not ready for unattended production use as published.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who might expose the defaults: the README documents `admin` as the initial password and `spider-panel-secret-key-v2` as the default session secret.

reviews.name: midday
reviews.verdict: Midday has an appealing product shape for independent workers, but this repository is a serious platform deployment rather than a weekend self-host.
reviews.skip_if: Operators seeking a compact self-hosted finance app: the README names Supabase, Railway, Vercel, Cloudflare, Trigger.dev, Resend, bank providers, analytics, payments, search, and AI services.

reviews.name: spacedrive
reviews.verdict: Spacedrive has an unusually coherent answer to file sprawl, especially its content identity, offline catalog, and permission model for agents.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to test against disposable data first: an open Windows report says v2 alpha.2 deleted a nonempty root-level folder named `tmp` when its volume was tracked.

reviews.name: linuxdo-idea-ui
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run linuxdo-idea-ui because the JavaScript userscript exposed no supported ecosystem and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not read Chinese: the README and interface description are Chinese, with no English guide linked.

reviews.name: OpenCut
reviews.verdict: Do not choose the rewritten OpenCut as a primary editor yet, because its maintainers do not make that claim.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs this rewritten codebase for paid editing work today: the README recommends OpenCut Classic for current use.

reviews.name: ComfyUI-ALLinONE-MinimaxH3
reviews.verdict: This is a smart control surface for people already paying the complexity cost of MiniMax H3 in ComfyUI.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners expecting one clone command to provide the models: the requirements list five large H3 model files, and some modes add more models or node packs.

reviews.name: obsidian-skills
reviews.verdict: Obsidian Skills is a forward-thinking toolkit for a very specific audience: developers integrating AI agents into their personal knowledge management.
reviews.skip_if: Casual Obsidian users looking for a simple, in-app AI writing assistant.

reviews.name: hexstrike-ai
reviews.verdict: HexStrike AI is a stunningly ambitious and powerful framework that offers a tangible glimpse into the future of AI-driven cybersecurity.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners in cybersecurity or programming.

reviews.name: TRELLIS.2
reviews.verdict: TRELLIS.2 is a landmark research project that produces arguably state-of-the-art results in image-to-3D generation.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners or hobbyists with consumer-grade GPUs, as the 24GB VRAM requirement and specific hardware recommendations are strict.

reviews.name: TelegramGroup
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run TelegramGroup because it has no supported code ecosystem or Dockerfile, so judge it as a 250 KB link directory rather than an open-source application.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a Telegram API library, bot framework, or runnable search engine: the repository is a Markdown directory with no detected programming language or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: holehe
reviews.verdict: Holehe still has a sharp, useful idea and an unusually broad module catalog, but its output is only as trustworthy as dozens of changing third-party flows.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs consistently current checks across every advertised service: the last repository push was in September 2024, while open reports and pull requests describe broken modules and fixes that have not landed.

reviews.name: minio
reviews.verdict: Do not choose this archived MinIO repository for a new production object store.
reviews.skip_if: New production storage deployments expecting an active open-source upstream: the repository says it is no longer maintained and GitHub marks it archived.

reviews.name: Antigravity
reviews.verdict: Antigravity is a narrowly targeted workaround, and its selective routing is less disruptive than sending the whole computer through a VPN.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the README describes a Windows program, while open requests ask for ports to those systems.

reviews.name: everything-claude-code
reviews.verdict: Do not install the WorldFlowAI snapshot as your default Claude Code toolkit.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants the maintained original project: this snapshot's README, plugin manifest, marketplace commands, and homepage all point to affaan-m/everything-claude-code, which GitHub now redirects to affaan-m/ECC.

reviews.name: skitter-creek-bath-salts
reviews.verdict: Use skitter-creek-bath-salts if you are doing serious platform-security research on disposable AMD Family 16h hardware and its unusually clear explanation is as valuable to you as the code.
reviews.skip_if: General developers, because this is research code rather than a normal utility Anyone using a daily-driver or production machine, because rewriting memory-controller behavior can crash or corrupt it Owners of newer AMD, Intel, ARM, or RISC-V systems expecting a ready-made…

reviews.name: typescript-go
reviews.verdict: Our source build stopped after 8 seconds because `go` was missing, and the repository itself is due for archival in September 2026, so new users should go straight to microsoft/TypeScript.
reviews.skip_if: New TypeScript contributors: the README says development and discussion have moved to microsoft/TypeScript, while this repository will be archived in September 2026.

reviews.name: Flowise
reviews.verdict: Do not start a new production system on the archived Flowise repository.
reviews.skip_if: New production adopters who expect vendor maintenance: the maintainers announced a code freeze, archived the repository on August 13, 2026, and set end of life for August 31.

reviews.name: personal-edge-proxy
reviews.verdict: Our harness could not run Personal Edge Proxy because it has no detected language ecosystem or Dockerfile, so treat it as an architecture note and sanitized configuration set, not verified software.
reviews.skip_if: English-only readers: the README and both topic guides are Chinese, with only the AI maintainer instructions written in English.

reviews.name: daytona
reviews.verdict: Daytona presents a powerful and comprehensive vision for AI agent infrastructure, but its open-source version is a ghost ship.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a production-ready, supported, and maintained solution.

reviews.name: browser-tools-mcp
reviews.verdict: Despite an impressive feature set and thousands of stars, BrowserTools MCP is a ghost ship.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a reliable, working tool for production or daily development.

reviews.name: Roo-Code
reviews.verdict: Roo Code is a ghost.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a reliable, actively maintained AI coding tool for professional or daily use.

reviews.name: outlook-auto-register
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 47 packages in 13 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but there was no test target, so the polished console sits on unverified account-creation code.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to create usable Outlook accounts in bulk: Microsoft Support explicitly says not to use programs, scripts, or bots to create Microsoft accounts.

reviews.name: cve-2026-41940-PoC
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 11 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but there was no test target, so this PoC is easy to prepare and unproven as a diagnostic.
reviews.skip_if: cPanel administrators looking for the safest exposure check: cPanel publishes its own patch versions and detection guidance, while this project performs exploitation and post-access actions.

reviews.name: grok-bot-0.18-reconstructed
reviews.verdict: Our install added 383 packages, but both the 3-second build and 3-second test run failed, so this reconstruction is research material rather than a dependable desktop-agent dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams needing a clean license chain: GitHub reports no license, NOTICE describes retained upstream boundaries, and issue 7 asks for licensing and derivative-work permission to be clarified.

reviews.name: fanqiang
reviews.verdict: Fanqiang is useful as a Chinese-language directory of circumvention approaches, not as a tidy package you can clone and build.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need English installation or troubleshooting documentation: the main README and most linked guides are written in Chinese.

reviews.name: learn
reviews.verdict: Our install attempt failed in 5 seconds inside `extensions/visual-tools/`, so Learn is best treated as a readable personal configuration for current pi users, not an install-and-forget tutor.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a standalone tutor: the repository is a `.pi` directory and requires the separate pi agent.

reviews.name: grok-1
reviews.verdict: Use Grok-1 when the object of study is Grok-1 itself.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a laptop or single-GPU chatbot: the README says the 314B-parameter model needs enough GPU memory, and the included runner configures an eight-device local mesh.

reviews.name: opencode
reviews.verdict: Do not adopt `opencode-ai/opencode` for new work.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone starting a new coding-agent setup: the first lines of the README say this repository is archived and direct users to Crush for ongoing development.

reviews.name: v4-flash-godmode-opencode-go
reviews.verdict: Do not choose this fork for a new deployment.
reviews.skip_if: New users seeking a maintained installation, because the project explicitly no longer evolves Production teams that need releases, a known license, and a stable support path English-only readers, because no English documentation is evidenced here Anyone wanting the newer standard…

reviews.name: deploy-vercel
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 66 packages into 81 MB, while the five-file project supplied no build or test target, so deploy-vercel asks you to trust security-sensitive network code without a verification suite.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for English setup or security documentation: the README is Chinese and does not provide an English guide.

reviews.name: node
reviews.verdict: Our Rust contract-sample build installed 4 packages, then failed in 34 seconds with 20 type errors, so the repository does not currently offer a dependable Rust contract starting point at commit `01e66db`.
reviews.skip_if: Contract developers who need a working Rust sample today: our build of `contract_samples/rust/` failed with 20 compiler errors.

reviews.name: DeepSeek-V4-J-Space-Capability-Realization-Report
reviews.verdict: The v2.0 repository ships 2 report files and no executable harness, raw task traces, or machine-readable results, so its score table is not decision-grade evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a model or agent stack from reproducible evidence: the v2.0 release lists only Chinese and English report files.

reviews.name: cloud-cost-optimization-hub
reviews.verdict: CCOH is an appealing shell for a cloud-cost product, not a trustworthy optimization platform yet.
reviews.skip_if: FinOps teams expecting real three-cloud billing: `gcp_service.go` and `azure_service.go` explicitly generate fixed daily sample costs, and issue #5 asks for the missing GCP Billing API integration.

reviews.name: wenai
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run wenai at commit a25b95b because it had no detected ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so none of its access, persistence, or image steps are verified here.
reviews.skip_if: Minors or anyone seeking non-adult role-play: the skill is explicitly for fictional consenting adults and contains explicit sexual workflows.

reviews.name: iready-tool
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run iReady Tool because it exposes no supported runnable ecosystem or Dockerfile, and the repository has 0 releases and 0 open issues or pull requests to substantiate compatibility.
reviews.skip_if: Students seeking legitimate help with i-Ready work: the tool is designed to falsify lesson completion, minutes, quizzes, and diagnostics, which can violate school rules and corrupt learning records.
